<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1229
Claimant:
Meghan Green
Adjuster:
Valerie Rodriguez
January 22, 2025
The claimant reported a left-turn collision at an intersection and said a vehicle coming straight through struck the
driver's side of their car. The claim was opened the same day and the file was assigned for review.
January 29, 2025
The driver is named on the policy, and the policy was in force at the time of the reported loss. Nothing in the
underwriting file suggests the vehicle damage predates the covearge start.
April 3, 2025
Police attended the scene and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. Two officers' notes are on file
and they match the claimant's first account.
May 11, 2025
Photos taken at the scene confirm several details of the reported impact. The vehicle damage is consistent with the
described angle and direction of the collision.
May 19, 2025
No independent witnesses have come forward, so the account rests on the claimant's statement, the photos, and the
police report. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.
May 21, 2025
The claimant reported neck pain shortly after the collision and was seen at an urgent care clinic. No earlier injury to
the same body area is known from the medical history provided.
July 1, 2025
The claimant has since added a few small details to the account, such as the position of the signal and the speed of
the other car. The core sequence of events has stayed the same across each retelling.
July 24, 2025
Treatment for the neck strain followed a usual course of physical therapy and medication. Reports show steady
improvement, and the treatment has tapered off as the patient recovered.
August 25, 2025
It is not yet clear whteher the neck injury came from this crash, as the medical records and the timing of symptoms
are still being reviewed. The file remains open pending the treating provider's causation opinion.
September 3, 2025
The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been dealing with the adjuster directly. The file will be
reviewed again once the remaining mdeical records are received.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
